live_brain: The live brain is the tilt_adapter (the intended new model: the deterministic chassis rules + a SMALL M1 ML tilt on top — the yellow line, book F). The ML's only job is to make the rules that already work a little better. Wired via src/brain/tilt_live.run_tilt_cutover, called from publish_artifacts.run_brain_cutover_night when engine=='tilt_adapter'.
retired_engine: native_two_stage is RETIRED (operator verdict 2026-06-23: 'bunk' — it discarded the working deterministic rules and built a from-scratch concentrated book that crashed; the only fix that helped just reproduced the deterministic result). It is no longer the live engine and is not branded canon. Kept in-tree only as a comparison line.
fail_safe: run_tilt_cutover has a hard abort-never-degrade: ANY error (inference fail, tilt exception, missing organ outputs) returns ok=False and the live path keeps the deterministic incumbent intents untouched. The deterministic rules are the safe floor.
rollback: Set engine to anything other than 'tilt_adapter' (or mode to 'shadow') and redeploy -> the live path falls back to the deterministic incumbent. The tilt only ever ADDS a small ML edit on top of the rules; it never replaces them.
non_assertion: Going live authorizes forward measurement; it does NOT assert the ML tilt has a dollar edge. The rent ladder (the bottom evaluation panel) measures, organ by organ, whether the ML is paying rent — currently ~zero. The tilt is live because the design is 'let the ML nudge the working rules', and the rent ladder grades it as we go.
